Pseudoxanthoma elasticum: Verhoeff-vanGieson stained sections: marked decrease or total absence of elastic fibres in both superficial and mid-dermis
Elastic fibres around the vessels in the affected areas: fragmented and markedly decreased
Haematoxylin and eosin stained section: faintly eosinophilic separated collagen fibers in the upper and mid-dermis
Lesions: whitish papules and depressed areas with central protrusion
Location of lesions: dorsum of fingers, forearms, distal portion of thighs, and calves
Lumbar lordosis, laxity in large joints, tibia vara, high-arched palate, and dental misalignment

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's presentation of whitish papules and depressed areas with central protrusion, along with the histopathological findings of decreased elastic fibers and fragmented collagen, are consistent with Pseudoxanthoma elasticum. The presence of systemic manifestations such as lumbar lordosis, joint laxity, and dental misalignment also supports this diagnosis.
